en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Garlic Chapter.
7. The Training Rule on Raw Grain.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, during the harvest season, the bhikkhunīs requested raw grain and brought it into the city;
at the gate, people said, "Give us a share, venerable ladies," and having obstructed them,
they released [the grain] only after being detained.
Then those bhikkhunīs went to the dwelling and reported this matter to the bhikkhunīs.
Those bhikkhunīs who were few in desires... [as before]... complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
"How can these bhikkhunīs request raw grain?"... [as before]...
“Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunīs are asking for raw grain?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
“How indeed, monks, could bhikkhunīs request raw grain? This, monks,
is neither for the purpose of inspiring faith in those without faith … [and so on] … And thus,
monks, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule:”

“Whatever nun, having requested raw grain, or having had it requested, or having roasted it, or having had it roasted, or having pounded it, or having had it pounded, or having cooked it, or having had it cooked, should eat it, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Whatever nun” means whichever nun... [and so on].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Raw grain" means:
Rice, paddy, barley, wheat, millet, panic seed, and small rice.
"Having known for oneself" means having known by oneself.
"Having requested" means having requested something else.
"Having roasted" means...
"Having roasted it oneself.
"Having had it roasted by another" means having had someone else roast it.
"Having pounded" means having pounded it oneself. "Having had it pounded" means...
[having had it pounded by another].
"Having had another pound it.
"Having cooked it" means having cooked it oneself.
"Having had it cooked" means having had someone else cook it.
If she accepts it with the thought, "I shall eat," there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
For every swallow, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
There is no offense if it is due to illness.
If she requests cooked food,
if she is insane,
or if she is a first-time offender.
The seventh training rule is finished.
